resources.string: Check official weather forecasts and flood warnings.
Identify whether your home is in a flood-prone area.
Know the nearest safe shelter and evacuation routes.
Download your area\'s offline map in FloodCue.
Save important emergency contact numbers.
Learn the local evacuation signals and instructions.
Discuss an emergency communication plan with your family.
Drinking water.
Ready-to-eat, non-perishable food.
First-aid kit.
Required medicines and prescriptions.
Flashlight and spare batteries.
Fully charged power bank and charging cables.
Battery-powered or hand-crank radio, if available.
Extra clothes and a raincoat.
Essential hygiene items and sanitary supplies.
Copies of identification and important documents in a waterproof bag.
Whistle for signalling rescuers.
Cash in small denominations.
Sturdy footwear.
Charge your phone fully.
Save emergency contacts in your phone.
Add family members\' contact details to FloodCue.
Add essential medical information, including allergies and required medicines.
Download the offline map for your area.
Verify that the downloaded map opens without internet.
Learn how to activate the emergency siren.
Understand how to send an SOS message.
Check whether your emergency SMS feature has the necessary permissions.
Carry a charged power bank if available.
Move important documents and valuables to a higher location.
Keep electrical appliances away from areas likely to flood.
Know how to switch off electricity and gas safely, if instructed and safe to do so.
Secure outdoor objects that could be swept away.
Move essential supplies above expected flood levels.
Keep doors and evacuation paths clear.
Move vehicles to higher ground if safe and permitted.
Follow official instructions about flood barriers and property protection.
Decide on a safe meeting point.
Identify an out-of-area family contact.
Ensure every family member knows how to contact the others.
Prepare essential supplies for infants, older adults and people with disabilities, if applicable.
Arrange necessary mobility aids and medical equipment.
Plan how to evacuate pets, if applicable.
Tell family members where the emergency go-bag is stored.
Explain what to do if family members become separated.
Follow instructions from local authorities.
Leave early if evacuation is advised.
Take your emergency go-bag.
Take essential medicines and identification documents.
Move to the designated safe shelter using an approved route.
Help children and people who need assistance, when safe.
Inform your designated emergency contact if possible.
Do not walk or drive through floodwater.
Do not wait to finish the checklist before evacuating.
